rules.rule: Get IServiceEndpointNotificationService from the service provider and call Execute(new EntityReference("serviceendpoint", id), context). Register asynchronously in the sandbox; a failed post reruns the whole plug-in, so it only prepares the context and posts. OperationId and OperationCreatedOn let consumers detect repeats.
signals: decide in code whether to post
post to an endpoint by ID
rules.trap: Sending with a Service Bus SDK and a stored connection string, or doing other work in the publisher

rules.topic: Publish with the Plug-in Registration Tool
rules.rule: Register the endpoint (webhook, queue, topic or event hub), then a step on it: message, table, filtering attributes, stage and mode, optionally images. No code; Service Bus and Event Hubs endpoints take asynchronous steps only, webhooks also synchronous.
signals: register a step on the endpoint
rules.trap: A custom plug-in for a filter the step already provides, or a step without filtering attributes

rules.rule: Webhook: URL plus HttpHeader, WebhookKey (query parameter code) or HttpQueryString, contract 8, 256 KB, 60 s. Service Bus queue or topic and Event Hubs: Register New Service Endpoint from a SAS connection string with Send only, designation and message format (JSON); 192 KB. One topic endpoint plus a subscription per consumer beats one endpoint per consumer.
rules.trap: Listen claim or managed identity for the endpoint; three queue endpoints where one topic serves

rules.rule: Block the save: synchronous plug-in, or a synchronous webhook if the rule must stay outside. Partner sometimes offline or every message must be processed: Service Bus queue; several consumers: topic. High-volume stream, replay, analytics: Event Hubs. Simple HTTPS endpoint, low volume: asynchronous webhook. No code: flow trigger. Own copy, deletions, own schedule: change tracking.
rules.trap: A webhook for a partner that is sometimes down; a topic where a stream with replay is asked

rules.rule: Enable Track changes; GET the entity set with $select and Prefer: odata.track-changes, store @odata.deltaLink, follow it later. Deletions are $deletedEntity entries with the id. $filter, $orderby, $expand and $top are refused. Changes are kept 7 days by default: an older token means a full reload. Apply changes, then store the token. The caller needs organization-level read.
rules.trap: Polling modifiedon (misses deletions), adding $filter, or raising retention to rescue an expired token

rules.rule: Key columns: decimal, whole number, single line of text, date and time, lookup or choice; up to 16 columns and 900 bytes, 10 keys per table, no column security. The index is built by a system job (Pending, In Progress, Active, Failed). Address rows as entityset(key='value') or with new Entity/EntityReference(table, key, value), which fills KeyAttributes, not Attributes.
signals: the key can't be used yet
rules.trap: Putting the key value in Attributes, unquoted text values, or expecting the key to work before the index is Active

rules.rule: UpsertRequest or a keyed PATCH without If-Match creates or updates idempotently (RecordCreated, or 201/200 with return=representation; 204 otherwise). If-Match: * means update only (404, nothing created); If-None-Match: * means create only (412). Leave key values out of the data. Send only the columns the source owns.
rules.trap: An upsert where an unknown key must not create a row

rules.rule: No auth, basic, API key, or OAuth 2.0 authorization code (generic or Entra ID with a per-connector redirect URI to register at the provider). Client credentials aren't supported: put a function you own in between. Entra ID can use the connector's managed identity instead of a client secret (single-tenant app, federated credential). Secrets as Key Vault environment variables.
rules.trap: Configuring the client credentials grant in the connector, or a client secret used as a shared API key

rules.rule: GA templates change calls without code: Set HTTP header, Set query string parameter, Route request (another path), Set host URL (host from expressions). Expressions @headers, @queryParameters, @connectionParameters; sections Request, Response, Failure; an empty operation list applies to all. Six reshaping templates and environment variables in policies are preview.
rules.trap: Custom code or new operations for what a GA template does

rules.rule: OpenAPI 2.0 file or URL below 1 MB (convert 3.0 and trim to the needed operations), a Postman collection, a connector from microsoft/PowerPlatformConnectors (Import from GitHub or pac connector create with apiDefinition and apiProperties), or the API Management export for Azure APIs.
rules.trap: Importing a 3.0 or oversized file, or pointing GitHub import at a partner file

rules.rule: For an API published in Azure API Management: APIs → Power Platform → Create a connector, choosing the environment, optionally a subscription key parameter or OAuth; update it from the same place. Azure Functions can be imported into API Management first or described by an OpenAPI definition.
rules.trap: Exporting and hand-editing the definition, or HTTP actions with keys in every flow

rules.rule: Use a function when the logic needs a secret, a grant connectors can't use, several sources, state, logging or private network access. Secure it with App Service authentication (Entra ID) so it can read the user from X-MS-CLIENT-PRINCIPAL; read secrets from Key Vault with its managed identity; answer HTTP within 230 seconds.
rules.trap: A function key as the connector's API key when the user must be known

rules.rule: summary titles an operation, x-ms-summary a parameter or property; x-ms-visibility important, advanced or internal (internal and required needs a default); x-ms-dynamic-values fills a list from another operation (operationId, parameters, value-collection, value-path, value-title); x-ms-capabilities testConnection; x-ms-trigger and x-ms-notification-url for triggers.
rules.trap: A static enum for values that change, or confusing summary with x-ms-summary

rules.rule: A Script class deriving from ScriptBase overrides ExecuteAsync and calls this.Context.SendAsync, then reshapes the request or response. Limits: 2 minutes, 1 MB, one script per connector, .NET Standard 2.0 with listed namespaces, no gateway, no logging; an empty scriptOperations list runs it for every operation.
rules.trap: Preview reshaping templates that can't compute, or repeating expressions in every flow
